Beta4: weapon prediction fixes

Predicted and server-confirmed rocket/hyperblaster impacts no longer produce duplicate audio, including server-first arrival. Rocket/rail sound sequences and stale projectile-to-server-entity bindings that could hide later flight visuals were fixed. Damage and confirmed hits remain server-authoritative. Optional rocketdiag start|mark|stop diagnostics are disabled by default and unnecessary for normal play.


Server history in beta 2

The modern browser now has History immediately after Favorites. It is shared across mods and stores address, time and mod in baseq2/q2pro-x/reconnect_history.json. The default is 10 unique servers; the range is 0–100, with 0 disabling history. Rejoining the already latest server does not change its record.

After a fresh launch, reconnect can use the last stored server. Optional automatic connection is off by default: it applies after remote online play, skips the intro/menu and yields to explicit startup commands. Single-player, a locally hosted server and demo playback retain normal startup.

VariableAccepted valuesDescription
cl_reconnect_history_limit0=disabled and cleared / 1=last server only / 2..100=MRU history (default 10)Global across all mods: maximum number of unique successfully played remote servers retained for manual reconnect and the History browser tab. Changing it applies immediately. 0 clears and disables disk history; 1 keeps only the last server; 10 is the default; 100 is the hard maximum.
cl_reconnect_last_server_auto0=normal startup (default) / 1=auto-connect eligible last remote serverOn an otherwise idle cold start, automatically connect to the newest successfully played remote server only when the previous play context was remote multiplayer. Default off. Any explicit +map, +connect, demo, URL or alias startup action takes priority.


Q2PRO-X network play

This guide covers everything that belongs to online play: connecting and the server browser, the advanced network settings, Ping Adaptation, LagHax, player and weapon prediction, weapon-part visibility, volumes and highlights.

Connection diagnosis — what is wrong, what to do about it and how to verify the result — has a guide of its own: Network God. Start there if the game feels bad and you do not know why.

3. Advanced Network: client UDP port autoprobe

Some routes/providers/servers can behave differently depending on the

client's UDP source port. Q2PRO-X 1.6 Beta 5 includes an experimental client-port

autoprobe.

Main cvar:

cl_net_clientport_autoprobe

Modes:

off - do nothing;
RTT - fast pre-connect challenge-RTT probe;
XQ3A - live-session scan over 20 slots, an xq3e-like adaptation.

Related cvars:

cl_net_clientport_autoprobe_time - safety watchdog;
cl_net_clientport_autoprobe_ports - candidate count for RTT mode;
cl_net_clientport_autoprobe_indicator - on-screen XQ3A scan indicator;
cl_net_clientport_autoprobe_verbose - detailed console log;
cl_net_clientport_autoprobe_settle_ms - pre-scan grace for XQ3A.

RTT mode

RTT mode opens independent probe sockets, sends challenges, and selects the

candidate by reply RTT. It is fast and safe, but its metric is not identical

to the gameplay ping shown in the HUD.

XQ3A mode

XQ3A mode is intentionally intrusive: during an active session, the socket may

rebind up to 20 times. While the scan runs, the player can feel jitter. Treat

it as a diagnostic tool, not a default for every match.

Recommendation:

normal players should keep it off;
use RTT for one-off connection tests;
use XQ3A only when you accept temporary scan jitter.

Related settings:

cl_laghax_hud_show_physics_params;
cl_laghax_hud_show_predict_runtime;
cl_laghax_hud_hide_deathmatch0;
cl_laghax_hud_hide_demo;
cl_laghax_maxms;
cl_laghax_maxwindow;
cl_laghax_minerror;
cl_laghax_ping_weight;
cl_laghax_jitter_weight;
cl_laghax_loss_weight;
cl_laghax_debt_weight;
cl_laghax_gap_weight.

Laghax does not move the server closer and does not change server authority.

It changes local presentation of networked movement so some micro-jitter feels

smoother.

For testing, enable the HUD, use adaptive mode, play for a few minutes, and

compare against off. If it feels too soft, lower the window/weights or use

fixed/off.


5. Weapon Predicts and Player Predict

Weapon predict draws part of the local firing feedback before server

confirmation arrives. This matters on high ping: you press fire, and the

client immediately shows local feedback.

Master:

cl_predict_weapons_enable.

Per-weapon toggles:

cl_predict_rockets;
cl_predict_rockets_explosion;
cl_predict_railgun;
cl_predict_shotgun;
cl_predict_super_shotgun;
cl_predict_machinegun;
cl_predict_chaingun;
cl_predict_blaster;
cl_predict_grenades;
cl_predict_hand_grenades;
cl_predict_hyperblaster.

Player predict:

cl_predict_player;
cl_predict_move_mode.

Adaptive ping gate:

cl_predict_ping_min_ms;
cl_predict_ping_dwell_sec.

When cl_predict_ping_min_ms is above 0, predicts are gated by ping and

dwell time. This avoids keeping the extra predicted layer active on low ping

where it may be unnecessary.

10. Practical profiles

Clean competitive baseline

modern server browser;
cl_laghax 0 or 2 after personal testing;
cl_predict_weapons_enable 1;
cl_predict_ping_min_ms 20;
cl_predict_ping_dwell_sec 5;
weapon FX visibility defaults;
cl_vis_players_mode team for TDM;
cl_net_clientport_autoprobe off.

High ping test

enable weapon predict;
enable player predict;
raise cl_predict_ping_min_ms only if the predicted layer is distracting at

low ping;

enable laghax HUD;
compare cl_laghax 0, 1, and 2 on the same server.

Problem route diagnostics

enable cl_net_clientport_autoprobe RTT;
try connect_autoport <server>;
if deeper testing is needed, use XQ3A with indicator and verbose log, but

not during an important match.


11. Russian input, transliteration, and /en translation

Q2PRO-X 1.6 Beta 5 covers two separate chat problems: safe Russian input/transliteration for Quake II console/chat, and a separate /en command that translates Russian text to English before you send it.

Setting / commandMeaning
cl_console_utf8_ruRussian display localization. It affects UI/hints rendering, but it is not the Russian-input switch.
cl_translit_x_style 0Transliterate Russian х as kh. Default.
cl_translit_x_style 1Transliterate Russian х as h if that style is preferred.
/en <text>Asynchronously translates Russian text to English through the active provider and replaces the current prompt. You still press Enter manually.
/en -team <text>Same workflow, prepared for team chat.
translate_statusPrints provider, URL, timeout, and key availability.
translate_reloadReloads the local translation secret/config file.
Transliteration preserves a leading / or \ and the command token, so say/say_team commands do not become plain chat text.
/en never sends automatically. The player sees the English result and decides whether to send it.
The default provider is q2prox, the hosted Q2PRO-X endpoint. It does not require a client API key.
Related provider cvars: cl_translate_provider, cl_translate_q2prox_url, cl_translate_google_url, cl_translate_deepl_url, cl_translate_azure_url, cl_translate_libre_url, cl_translate_custom_url, cl_translate_timeout_ms.
Secrets for third-party providers live in baseq2/q2pro-x/translate.local. This file is not archived, not echoed, and must not be shipped in public packages.
Text translated through /en is sent to the configured provider. Do not use it for private keys, passwords, or other secrets.
Only one translation request is in flight at a time. On timeout or failure, the prompt remains unchanged so the message is not lost.

Practical workflow

1. Type /en привет, идём на railgun.

1. Wait for the prompt to be replaced with the English result.

1. Review the text and press Enter if you want to send it.

1. For team chat, use /en -team ... or your usual say_team workflow if it is already in the prompt.

Troubleshooting

translate_status reports an invalid provider: check cl_translate_provider.
Translation does not arrive: check cl_translate_timeout_ms, the hosted endpoint, or your third-party provider.
The prompt was not replaced: you may have edited it after starting /en; the client does not overwrite new user input.
Need ASCII immediately without an online provider: use Russian input/transliteration rather than /en.



12. Ping Adaptation

12.1. Why it exists

Ping Adaptation deliberately adds delay to outgoing game data so that your final ping stays near a chosen value.

It exists for exactly two things:

to level the conditions against an opponent whose ping is noticeably higher;
to practise under conditions you want to get used to.
It does not reduce ping. The value sets the final ping, not the addition. With a real 10 ms and a target of 30 ms, about 20 ms is added; if the real ping is already above the target, nothing is added.

The layer creates no packet loss and is compatible with LagHax, prediction, fixed movement and the existing movement-feel modes.

12.2. Where it lives

Menu path: Main menu → Online Play Setup → Ping Adaptation

Ping Adaptation

TypeSectionRowVariable or targetWhat it does

The value is the FINAL ping, not an addition: real 10 with a target of 30 adds about 20, and a real ping already above the target adds nothing. Applies immediately. [Off / Manual / Automatic]
ListModeAutomatic sourcecl_ping_adapt_auto_sourceWhere Automatic takes its target: a configured range, or the active opposing players (OpenTDM: the other team; OpenFFA: the other active players). Spectators and you are always excluded. Applies immediately. [Range / Players]

SliderManualTarget pingcl_ping_adapt_manual_msAbsolute target ping for Manual mode. A target below your real ping simply adds nothing. Applies immediately.

SliderPlayersOffsetcl_ping_adapt_offset_msSigned offset from the opponents' ping. Target = opponent ping + offset. Example: opponent 40 with offset -10 gives a target of 30. Applies immediately.
SliderPlayersMinimum differencecl_ping_adapt_min_difference_msAdaptation starts only when your real ping is below the opponents' ping by at least this much. Example: opponent 40 and 15 here leaves a real ping of 30 alone. Applies immediately.

12.3. Three modes

ModeWhat it does
OffNothing is added; this is the default
ManualHolds your own target
AutomaticTakes the target from the selected source

12.4. Two automatic sources

Range. You set a lower and an upper bound. Adaptation works only while the real ping is below the lower bound; one target is then chosen inside the band and held steadily.

Players. The target is taken from the active opponents:

in team play the other team is used;
in free-for-all play the other active players are used;
spectators and you yourself are always excluded.

The target is computed as "the opponent's ping plus the offset". The offset is signed: with an opponent at 40 ms and an offset of −10 ms, the target is 30 ms.

12.5. When adaptation stays out of the way

The Minimum difference setting protects you from needless intervention: adaptation engages only when your real ping is lower than the opponents' by at least that much. With an opponent at 40 ms and a minimum difference of 15 ms, your real ping of 30 ms is left as it is.

Maximum final ping is a hard ceiling on the target in automatic mode. It applies to both automatic sources and never to manual mode: you set a manual target yourself and you own it.

12.6. How often the target is recomputed

The check interval decides how often the target and the opponent roster are recomputed. Requests to the server are coalesced and never sent more than once per second: adaptation does not create a storm of queries.

12.7. Observing and verifying

CommandWhat it shows
ping_adapt_infoThe complete current state: the real and adapted ping, the target, the added delay, the opponents and the queue
ping_adapt_resetRestarts the measurement and roster tracking without changing settings; packets already queued are sent in order first

A separate switch logs adaptation events to the console — mode changes, target changes, roster updates — and never prints per packet:

VariableAccepted valuesDescription
cl_ping_adapt_debug0=off (default) / 1=log ping adaptation events to consoleEvent-based diagnostic logging for Ping adaptation: mode transitions, target changes, roster invalidations, capacity fail-open and connection-generation resets. Never prints per packet. 0 = off (default) and costs nothing; the full current state is always available on demand through the ping_adapt_info command.

12.8. Returning to ordinary play

Returning is simply switching the mode off. No rollback of settings is needed: adaptation changes none of your other network parameters, it only delays sending. Once it is off, no delay is added any more.

Changing servers restarts the measurement and roster tracking: a decision from the previous server is never carried over to the next one.

12.9. How it relates to the other systems

SystemHow it relates
Network GodShows and accounts for adaptation, but never enables it, changes its target or adjusts its mode
LagHaxWorks independently; adaptation neither cancels nor replaces it
PredictionWorks independently; the server remains authoritative
Jitter ShieldA different job: it smooths the display of other players rather than delaying your sending
Network LabAlso spoils the network deliberately, but for practice and tests; the two never delay the same packet twice

In the Network God overview the real ping stays a separate figure, the added delay is shown separately, and the final ping reflects the sum the client works with.

12.10. Mod and server boundaries

The Players source relies on the server and the mod actually reporting the roster and the participants' pings. Team and free-for-all play are recognised from the mod's data. If a mod does not supply enough information, the Players source simply cannot name a target — use the Range source or manual mode in that case.

Adaptation is entirely client-side: it changes no protocol, requires no server support and affects no other player.

12.11. The complete setting list

VariableAccepted valuesDescription
cl_ping_adapt_mode0=off (default) / 1=manual / 2=automaticPing adaptation master. 0 = off (default): no send adapter, no queue, no probes, no roster scans and no added latency at all. 1 = Manual: hold an absolute target ping of cl_ping_adapt_manual_ms. 2 = Automatic: pick the target from cl_ping_adapt_auto_source (a configured range, or the active opposing players on OpenTDM / OpenFFA). The target is ABSOLUTE, never added on top of your real ping: with a real 10 ms and a target of 30 the client injects about 20 ms, and if your real ping is already 40 nothing is added. Latency is produced by FIFO-delaying complete outgoing datagrams, so no packet is dropped, reordered or rewritten.
cl_ping_adapt_auto_source0=range (default) / 1=playersWhere Automatic mode gets its target. 0 = Range: if your real ping is below cl_ping_adapt_range_min_ms, one target is chosen at random inside the configured band and then held stable for the whole session — it is not rerolled per packet or per evaluation. 1 = Players: follow the active opposing roster (OpenTDM: the other team, one player in duel and the mean in TDM; OpenFFA: the mean of all other active players). Spectators and you are always excluded. Range works on any mod; Players needs an exact roster adapter and otherwise adds nothing.
cl_ping_adapt_manual_ms0 .. 1000 ms, default 30Absolute target ping for Manual mode, in milliseconds. The client injects max(0, target - real RTT); it can never make a link faster, so a target below your real ping simply adds nothing and the state reads baseline limited. The automatic cap cl_ping_adapt_max_ms deliberately does NOT apply here — a manual target is your explicit instruction.
cl_ping_adapt_range_min_ms0 .. 1000 ms, default 20Lower bound of the Automatic/Range band, in milliseconds. Range adapts only while your real ping is BELOW this value; at or above it nothing is added, because latency cannot be removed. If minimum and maximum are entered reversed they are normalized (swapped) deterministically and ping_adapt_info shows the effective pair.
cl_ping_adapt_range_max_ms0 .. 1000 ms, default 30Upper bound of the Automatic/Range band, in milliseconds. Both bounds are additionally capped by cl_ping_adapt_max_ms; if that cap is below the configured minimum, the effective choice collapses to the cap.
cl_ping_adapt_check_interval_ms250 .. 10000 ms, default 1000How often Automatic mode recomputes its target and refreshes the opposing roster, in milliseconds. Server status probes are coalesced and never sent faster than once per second, so a shorter interval simply reuses the newest sample instead of adding traffic. Peer pings older than max(5000, 3 x interval) are treated as stale and adaptation falls back to zero added delay.
cl_ping_adapt_offset_ms-200 .. 200 ms, default 0Signed offset applied to the opposing players' reference ping in Automatic/Players mode: the target is (opponent ping + offset), then capped by cl_ping_adapt_max_ms. Negative values aim below the opponent, positive values above. Example: opponent 40, offset -10 gives a target of 30.
cl_ping_adapt_min_difference_ms0 .. 500 ms, default 15Minimum gap that must exist between your real ping and the opposing reference ping before Automatic/Players adapts at all. Adaptation runs only while real < (opponent - this value); otherwise nothing is added. Example: opponent 40 and a minimum difference of 15 means a real ping of 30 is left alone, while a real ping of 10 is adapted.
cl_ping_adapt_max_ms1 .. 1000 ms, default 200Hard ceiling on the final target ping in Automatic mode, in milliseconds. It applies to both automatic sources (Range and Players) and never to Manual. If the computed target exceeds it the target is clamped and ping_adapt_info reports it as capped.

SliderPackets & syncServer updates / seccl_updateratecl_updaterate: requested server updates per second (10..30 typical). Some servers cap it. Applies immediately.
ListPackets & syncAsync modecl_asynccl_async: 0 = synchronous client/render loop; 1 = asynchronous render loop (default). 2 = Asynchronous render loop with GPU sync fence where supported. Applies immediately. [Sync / Async / Async + GPU sync]
TogglePackets & syncInstant packetcl_instantpacketcl_instantpacket: send a usercmd packet immediately after a button press instead of waiting for the next tick. Reduces input latency by up to one packet interval. Applies immediately.
SectionUDP port autoprobeUDP port autoprobe
ListUDP port autoprobeAuto-select client UDP portcl_net_clientport_autoprobeAuto-select the client UDP port: off, RTT (fast pre-connect challenge-RTT probe), or Full scan (live-session scan over 20 candidate ports). Applies immediately. [off / RTT / Full scan]
SliderUDP port autoprobeAuto-port safety watchdogcl_net_clientport_autoprobe_timeSafety watchdog (0.1..180 s) that aborts probing if it runs too long. RTT finishes early; a full-scan run wants 60..180 s, below ~30 s warns. Applies immediately.
SliderUDP port autoprobeRTT candidate countcl_net_clientport_autoprobe_portsRTT candidate port count (2..60). Does not apply to Full scan (fixed 20 slots). Wider sweeps don't slow RTT. Default 6. Applies immediately.
ToggleUDP port autoprobeFull-scan indicatorcl_net_clientport_autoprobe_indicatorShow a blinking AUTO-PORT SCAN indicator while the full scan runs (no effect on RTT). Applies immediately.
ToggleUDP port autoprobeAutoport console logcl_net_clientport_autoprobe_verbosePrint autoport progress to the console (slot switches, samples, winner, abort). Off = runs silently. Applies immediately.
SliderUDP port autoprobeFull-scan pre-scan gracecl_net_clientport_autoprobe_settle_msOptional grace window (0..10000 ms) before the full scan applies its first slot. Raise only on slow-precache mods. Counts inside the watchdog. Applies immediately.

The scanner briefly owns the connection while it runs, and Ping Adaptation stands down for its duration. That is deliberate: two mechanisms must not govern sending at the same time.

Favourite servers are global across all mods. Scanning shows live tabs and stops with the same button that starts it. The selected tab is remembered between launches.


15. Mod-dependent settings and skin override

Settings that depend on the current mod are stored separately from the global configuration file. Where each thing is written is explained in the cvars and cvar browser guide.
The skin override lets you locally view yourself and other players with preferred models and skins, without changing server logic.
That matters in team and free-for-all play, where you may want one skin for yourself and a different common look for everyone else.
Configuration profiles are available for baseq2, OpenTDM and OpenFFA: a profile changes the live controls and settings without overwriting the managed Q2PRO-X configs, and it is removed on a mod change.


Personal frag messages

Open Frag Messages in Network Play settings. All controls in this section are global (G). They change only your client, not your nickname colour on other players' clients. Opponent-name highlighting in the console is enabled by default. Personal kill and death notifications beneath the crosshair are off by default and enabled independently. Select a named palette colour for the opponent: it matches in the console and notification. Other text has a separate colour. Chat formatting is unaffected.

Messages use the console font with a bold nickname; Russian and English text have matching proportions. Kill notices fade away, while the killer's name remains until actual respawn. A weapon is shown only when the server message identifies it reliably. At most three lines are displayed together.

Adjust position, scale, kill-display time, line count, text colour and background opacity. fragfeed_preview previews the look without a gameplay event; fragfeed_reset restores this section's factory values. Known Quake II, OpenFFA, OpenTDM and OpenTDM-X message formats are supported. Other players' events while spectating or watching demos are not attributed to you. Ambiguous messages do not become invented personal kills.

Frag Messages settings in English.

Example notification and highlighted opponent name in the console.

The screenshots show a user's choices: mint nickname, red text, scale 1.20, offset 184 and 9.10 seconds. These are examples, not factory defaults.
